issues.body: DeployOnlyInertnessTests still skips every '/'-suffixed entry, including deploy/, while its class docstring says every entry is proven not read by Rust-CI workflows and that later wiring cannot silently become unsound. ci_audit_inputs.py detects crate source reads and test_no_crate_lives_under_a_deploy_entry detects manifests, but neither detects a Rust workflow shell step that directly consumes a file beneath deploy/. The added explanation therefore does not close the prior round's coverage gap.
issues.fix_hint: Add a structural check for direct deploy/ references in the enumerated Rust-CI workflows, with a narrow way to ignore comments/prose, or narrow the class/test claims to state explicitly that workflow-level directory references are convention-audited rather than live-enforced.
issues.title: Directory-prefix inertness guard still does not inspect workflow references

verdict.summary: The deploy-only and inert-mixed classification remains fail-closed for any engine path, and the workflow wiring tests pin all three merge-group consumers to the classifier's exact inert-class set. The prior round's minor test-strength concern remains materially unchanged: the new comments explain why deploy/ directory entries are skipped, but the two cited checks cover crate membership and crate source reads, not direct shell/workflow consumption of a deploy/ file. No blocker or major correctness, soundness, or security issue was found.
